summary: A model with enough freedom can pass through every training point. Then it meets data it has not seen.
headline: A model that memorises
overview: A curve with enough freedom can pass close to every training dot. Training error falls and falls.
Then you show it points it has never seen. That score is the one that counts.

break.label: Break it
break.explains: Press the button to add freedom one degree at a time. Training error keeps dropping while the error on unseen points turns around and climbs.

check.question: Training error keeps falling as you add model freedom. Test error rises. What is happening?

realLife: Fraud models that look perfect on last year's data and fail on this month's are often overfit.
data: Fourteen training points and sixty held-out test points, all from one sine wave with noise. Results depend heavily on this small sample, so another draw would put the turning point elsewhere. Degrees stop at 9 to keep the log-scale chart readable.
maths: Training error is the same sum over the points used to fit. The gap between them grows as the number of free weights approaches the number of points.
